diagnosis.overview: The worker consistently bypasses actual retrieval from provided source files (Excel, .xlsb, large CSVs), fabricating plausible but incorrect numbers (e.g., hallucinated 115 voters, 30,761.89 equity, 42-minute trip) instead of reading and computing on real data.
diagnosis.root_cause: The worker consistently bypasses actual retrieval from provided source files (Excel, .xlsb, large CSVs), fabricating plausible but incorrect numbers (e.g., hallucinated 115 voters, 30,761.89 equity, 42-minute trip) instead of reading and computing on real data.
diagnosis.general_mechanism: 1. Insert a mandatory pre-computation guardrail in the system prompt: 'Before any calculation, read the source file values explicitly and print the extracted numbers. If reading fails, report the error and do not proceed with guessed data.' 2. Wire up a robust file reader tool (or bind the existing library) that can handle .xlsb, large Excel files, and multi-sheet workbooks without truncation or corruption, so retrieval never silently fails. 3. Add middleware that imposes a hard iteration/time limit on computational loops and, on breach, forces the agent to switch to a closed-form or simpler approximation instead of infinite looping.
